name: Le Tigre
label: Mr. Lady
lede: A band named in 1994 before it existed, launched from a solo record on a label that started with $35, and still hard to walk past on a dance floor.

eras.title: A band name in search of a band
eras.text: Kathleen Hanna keeps a list of imaginary bands. When Bikini Kill ends in 1998, one of them gets members.

years.h: Hanna invents Le Tigre, one of many bands that don't exist yet
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] makes up hypothetical bands around 1994. Le Tigre is one of them, and it's the one that gets built.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album)
years.h: Bikini Kill ends; the Julie Ruin solo project turns into a trio
years.p: Hanna recruits Johanna Fateman, whom she'd met at a Bikini Kill show, and the artist [[Sadie Benning|ad77bd6f-90e3-439d-b990-bfed508686a8]] to turn her solo material into a live band.
years.xp:
Hanna and Fateman had already played together in a band called the Troublemakers, and Hanna had worked with Benning on video for her solo album as [[The Julie Ruin|357ffd02-384f-4dbd-abcd-5f1bcb616ef9]]. The plan was a live format for the solo songs; it became a collaboration instead.

The trio traded song ideas on cassette while Benning was based in Chicago, then signed with Mr. Lady Records. Hanna called the label "a logical choice" for its political commitment.

eras.title: Drum machines and a slide projector
eras.text: The first record arrives on a feminist label started on $35, and the line-up rearranges itself around what the road demands.

years.h: JD Samson starts as a roadie who runs the slideshow by hand
years.p: [[JD Samson|fd42790a-2d28-4564-9da9-9b3686597ec8]] joins the crew in September 1999. The budget can't stretch to anything automated, so Samson advances the slides during the set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album) · Wikipedia: Mr. Lady Records
years.h: Le Tigre arrives on Mr. Lady, a label started on $35
years.p: Produced with Chris Stamey of the dB's and built from Alesis drum machines, a Farfisa organ, samplers and turntables.
years.xp:
Fateman described the gear choice as "girl-punk scorn for that particular strain of male expertise" tied to electronic music. Mr. Lady was founded by Tammy Rae Carland and Kaia Wilson, and Wilson has said it started with "$35 and a lotta...faith".

Robert Christgau wrote that Hanna "reinvents punk again." Spin gave it 9/10, and Pitchfork put it 43rd on its 2022 list of the best 1990s albums.

years.h: Deceptacon opens the record and comes with a dance
years.p: The opener riffs on Barry Mann's 1961 single "Who Put the Bomp" and spawns a crowd choreography known as the aerobicon.

years.h: Hot Topic, the album's only single, is a reading list you can dance to
years.p: The song name-checks women and LGBTQ+ artists and activists; Hanna compared it to a college syllabus. A sister track, My My Metrocard, goes after New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani's quality-of-life policing.

q: JD added an undeniable flair and charisma to the live show.
years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album) · Wikipedia: Sadie Benning
years.h: Benning can't tour, so Samson becomes the third member
years.p: Benning steps away to focus on filmmaking and Samson is made permanent.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page dates the change to 2000 and says Benning left to focus on film; the album page says Benning couldn't tour behind the record. Benning's own page gives 2001 as the departure year.

Benning went on to a career in video, painting and sculpture, with work in the collections of MoMA and the Whitney.

eras.title: Feminist Sweepstakes and a festival fight
eras.text: Second record, second line-up, one very public argument about who a women's festival is for.

years.h: Feminist Sweepstakes, cut in Chapel Hill with Samson on board
years.p: Recorded at Modern Recording in Chapel Hill with Chris Stamey and the band; the first album as a trio of Hanna, Fateman and Samson.
years.xp:
F.Y.R. draws on Shulamith Firestone's The Dialectic of Sex, and Dyke March 2001 is built from field recordings of New York's Dyke March. Keep on Livin' turned up again in the 2019 Jessica Jones finale.

Metacritic lists it at 78/100; Christgau and Entertainment Weekly both gave it an A-. Samson has said the title came from imagining what a feminist Easter basket might look like.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Mr. Lady Records
years.h: Le Tigre plays Michigan Womyn's Music Festival and takes the heat
years.p: The festival's womyn-born womyn policy excluded trans women; Wikipedia reports the band and the Butchies received criticism and death threats for playing it in 2001 and 2005.
years.xp:
Mr. Lady Records took its own backlash in 1999 for backing the festival, with Camp Trans and others boycotting. Wilson said at the time that transgender and transsexual people are an important part of the queer community.

Samson, who identifies as genderqueer, later said publicly (2013, on Tumblr) that they would not take part until all self-identified women were welcome. The festival closed in 2015.

years.h: Wordy Rappinghood with Chicks on Speed and Tina Weymouth
years.p: [[Chicks on Speed|4da58f86-c7fb-4837-9ef5-423f122d2d15]] cover a Tom Tom Club song with Le Tigre, Miss Kittin, Kevin Blechdom, ADULT.'s Nicola Kuperus and Tom Tom Club's Tina Weymouth; it reaches number 5 on the Belgian Dance Chart and 66 in the UK.

eras.title: The major-label experiment
eras.text: Tired, and curious whether a feminist band could survive on a Universal subsidiary, Le Tigre finds out.

q: It was time for a change for us.
years.src: Wikipedia: This Island (Le Tigre album) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band)
years.h: Le Tigre signs to Strummer, a Universal Records subsidiary
years.p: Hanna called it a make-or-break move for a band worn down by touring.
years.xp: Hanna also said she wanted feminist perspectives in mainstream spaces, and that she was bored doing the same thing over and over.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Mr. Lady Records
years.h: Mr. Lady closes; Le Tigre reissues its own back catalog
years.p: With the label gone, the band starts Le Tigre Records to keep the first two albums in print, distributed by Touch and Go.

years.h: This Island: the major-label record they made at home
years.p: Recorded from 2002 to 2004 in home studios around Manhattan, mostly on Pro Tools, with Nick Sansano producing and Ric Ocasek producing one track, Tell You Now.
years.xp:
The home studios were paid for out of touring money, so there were no studio deadlines and no label in the room. New Kicks samples Susan Sarandon and Al Sharpton from New York's 2003 anti-war protests.

Wikipedia reports it peaked at number 130 on the Billboard 200 and sold 90,000 copies by 2008. Metacritic has it at 66/100.

years.h: TKO on Conan
years.p: Le Tigre takes the This Island single TKO to late-night TV, footage of which survives online.

years.h: Le Tigre goes on a long hiatus
years.p: Touring exhaustion after This Island and three people's separate projects put the band on ice.

eras.title: Hiatus, with cameos
eras.text: No band, but the songs keep turning up, in a pop record, a Pussy Riot set and a documentary.

years.h: Le Tigre reunites to produce Christina Aguilera's My Girls
years.p: [[Christina Aguilera|b202beb7-99bd-47e7-8b72-195c8d72ebdd]] brings in Le Tigre, with [[Peaches|270acfee-1fbe-413e-a0a8-6a35a8b3b66c]] guesting, for a track on her album Bionic. Hanna's next band is [[The Julie Ruin|357ffd02-384f-4dbd-abcd-5f1bcb616ef9]].

yt: Deceptacon clip, Who Took the Bomp?
years.h: Who Took the Bomp? puts the 2004 tour on screen
years.p: The tour documentary Who Took the Bomp? Le Tigre on Tour, released by Oscilloscope, screens at San Francisco's Frameline festival.

years.h: Fateman and Samson play Deceptacon with Pussy Riot
years.p: At a Vice magazine concert in 2014 the pair perform it with [[Pussy Riot|631e3bc5-428a-432b-87f7-5d357a007fc0]]; the two groups reunite in 2015 to make material for Netflix's House of Cards.

eras.title: Back, and a lawsuit
eras.text: A campaign song, a copyright fight over the debut's opener, then the first tour in eighteen years.

years.h: I'm With Her backs Hillary Clinton, with a video
years.p: After a September announcement of a one-off, Le Tigre puts out the song and a video supporting Clinton's presidential campaign.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album)
years.h: Barry Mann says Deceptacon owes him a song
years.p: Mann, writer of 1961's Who Put the Bomp, claims infringement; Hanna and Fateman countersue in October and settle in November.
years.xp: Hanna and Fateman argued that the song's use of the bomp line was transformative critique, not copying. The case ended in a confidential settlement agreement with no public admission of liability.

years.h: This Ain't No Picnic is the first festival slot
years.p: Le Tigre, announced in December 2021 for the festival, returns to a big stage.

yt: Hot Topic, Albert Hall Manchester, June 2023
years.h: First tour in 18 years, and it mostly sells out
years.p: The band announces European and North American dates. By June they're at Manchester's Albert Hall playing Hot Topic.
